suggestions.title: Weigh in this morning — three mornings dark, and every gauge is flying on Friday's data

rationale.science: Body-comp decisions here run off a 14-day robust rate, not a reading — one read is noise around a slow trend, and missing mornings widen the error bar rather than pause it. When a rate looks off, check the logging before blaming the metabolism (Alhassan 2008).
rationale.data: Last read: Friday's 165.0. Saturday, Sunday and this morning are blank, the forecast has printed 163.9 three days running, sleep stops Wednesday night, and Sunday has no food logged at all. Behind the gap sit three estimate days — 3,200 / 4,000 / 3,000, all high sodium, Friday with 14 on the alcohol line. The rate tonight is 1.2 ± 0.89 lb/wk — the error bar is wider than your whole 1.0–1.4 band.
rationale.relationship: Everything downstream runs off the trend — the rate, the 20-day maintenance fit (now reading 2,672 on party-day arithmetic), the band, and the auto-pilot that tightened 136 calories on Saturday. You shipped the staleness safeguard and the confidence gate last night; those guards can flag a frozen rate, but only the scale unfreezes it. One ritual — scale, last night's sleep, Sunday's two numbers — and two mornings re-decide all of it on real data.

suggestions.predict: The first read back comes in high — mid-to-high 160s is an estimate, not a promise — then gives back roughly a pound a morning for three or four mornings, the same shape as 7/12 through 7/15, settling near the mid-164s the trend already holds. The test: reads gains 8/3 and 8/4, and the forecast trend moves off 163.9.
